set.dnssec.actionsDisabled: No permission for DNSSEC changes (read-only zone access or server set to “Save: No”)
set.dnssec.addKeyAlgoWarn: New algorithm: create the key active and NOT published first, and publish it only after the zone’s largest TTL – otherwise strict resolvers treat the zone as bogus.
set.dnssec.addKeyIntro: For a normal key change use the rollover assistant. Here you create individual keys for special cases, e.g. an algorithm change.
set.dnssec.algoHintEd: Ed25519/Ed448 need a PowerDNS build with a suitable crypto library. If support is missing, PowerDNS reports an error when creating the key.
set.dnssec.algoHintRsa: RSA produces much larger responses. Only choose it if your registrar does not support ECDSA.
set.dnssec.alreadyEnabled: DNSSEC was already active for this zone – nothing was changed.
set.dnssec.bumpSerialHint: Master zone: secondaries using AXFR only pick up the changed keys with a higher serial.
set.dnssec.confirmActivate: Activate key {{id}} ({{type}}, tag {{tag}})? The zone will additionally be signed with this key.
set.dnssec.confirmDeactivate: Deactivate key {{id}} ({{type}}, tag {{tag}})? It stops signing but stays published.
set.dnssec.confirmDelete: Permanently delete key {{id}} ({{type}}, tag {{tag}})? This cannot be undone.
set.dnssec.confirmPublish: Publish key {{id}} ({{type}}, tag {{tag}}) in the DNSKEY RRset?
set.dnssec.confirmUnpublish: Remove key {{id}} ({{type}}, tag {{tag}}) from the DNSKEY RRset? Resolvers can then no longer verify signatures made with it.
set.dnssec.denialNsec3Hint: Makes listing all names of the zone (zone walking) harder. Default per RFC 9276: 0 iterations, no salt.
set.dnssec.denialNsecHint: Simpler and slightly faster, but allows listing all names of the zone.
set.dnssec.disableConfirmCheckbox: I removed the DS records at the registrar and waited for the TTL.
set.dnssec.disablePeersNote: Other servers with their own database ({{servers}}) remain unchanged.
set.dnssec.disableRectifyWarn: Note: rectify after disabling reported an error: {{error}}
set.dnssec.disableStep1: Remove the DS record(s) at your registrar (currently: tag {{tags}}).
set.dnssec.disableStep2: Wait for the TTL of the DS in the parent zone (usually 1 to 24 hours; if unsure, 24 hours). Only then do resolvers forget the DS.
set.dnssec.disableStep3: Only then disable here. The other way round, validating resolvers return SERVFAIL – the domain is then effectively unreachable.
set.dnssec.disableWhat: Disabling deletes all keys of this zone on “{{server}}” and removes the NSEC3 parameters.
set.dnssec.dnskeyCheckConfirm: I have checked: all authoritative nameservers serve the new key.
set.dnssec.dnskeyCheckPending: Not checked (the automatic propagation check will follow). Check yourself that every authoritative nameserver serves the new key (tag {{tag}}), e.g. with: dig +dnssec DNSKEY {{zone}} @<nameserver>
set.dnssec.dsStatusUnpublishedActive: active but not published – do not register yet
set.dnssec.enableIntro: PowerDNS creates the keys and signs the zone live from now on. Afterwards you add the DS record at your registrar – only then is the chain of trust complete.
set.dnssec.errIterations: Please enter a whole number between 0 and {{max}}.
set.dnssec.errSalt: Invalid salt: hex characters only, even count (max. 510 characters).
set.dnssec.followNotifyError: NOTIFY failed: {{error}} – the change is saved; secondaries fetch it at the next refresh.
set.dnssec.followSerialError: Serial not increased: {{error}} – the key change is saved anyway.
set.dnssec.forceConfirm:
Safety check: {{reason}}

Proceed anyway? Validating resolvers may then treat the zone as bogus (SERVFAIL).
set.dnssec.hint.activeUnpublished: At least one active key is not published. That is only normal during an algorithm rollover.
set.dnssec.hint.algorithmRollover: Keys with different algorithms exist (algorithm rollover). Finish it via the key table.
set.dnssec.hint.apiRectifyOff: API-RECTIFY is off for this zone. After changes via the API the NSEC/NSEC3 chain can become stale. Save the NSEC settings once to switch it on.
set.dnssec.hint.deprecatedAlgorithm: Algorithm {{algorithm}} is deprecated (RFC 8624). Plan a switch to ECDSAP256SHA256.
set.dnssec.hint.keysInactiveOnly: Keys exist but none is active – the zone is not signed. Activate a key, or delete the keys and set up DNSSEC again.
set.dnssec.hint.multipleActiveSep: Several KSK/CSK are active – normal during a rollover. The registrar should then list the DS of both keys.
set.dnssec.hint.noActiveSep: No active KSK/CSK: the DS at the registrar cannot point to a signing key. Validating resolvers return SERVFAIL once a DS is registered.
set.dnssec.hint.nsec3IterationsHigh: NSEC3 uses {{iterations}} iterations – many resolvers treat that as insecure. Please lower it to 0.
set.dnssec.hint.nsec3IterationsNonzero: NSEC3 uses {{iterations}} additional iteration(s). RFC 9276 recommends 0.
set.dnssec.hint.nsec3Salt: NSEC3 uses a salt. RFC 9276 recommends not using a salt.
set.dnssec.hint.peersDivergent: On {{servers}} this zone has different DNSSEC keys. Separate databases with different keys cause validation failures – the keys must be synchronised manually (see docs). Right after a change, shared databases may show this briefly.
set.dnssec.hint.peersUnreachable: These servers could not be checked: {{servers}}.
set.dnssec.hint.peersUnsigned: On {{servers}} this zone is not signed. Once the DS is registered, answers from these servers fail validation.
set.dnssec.hint.presignedZone: Presigned zone: signatures come from the primary, keys are not managed here.
set.dnssec.hint.publishedUnsupported: PowerDNS {{version}} does not support the “published” flag (4.3 or later needed). Inactive keys are always published there; publish/unpublish is disabled.
set.dnssec.hint.rolloverInProgress: A key rollover is in progress ({{phase}}). Open the rollover assistant to continue.
set.dnssec.hint.secondariesSerial: Master zone: secondaries that transfer the signed zone via AXFR only pick up new keys after a serial increase. The panel increases the serial after key changes and sends a NOTIFY (can be switched off in the dialogs).
set.dnssec.hint.secondaryZoneSigning: Secondary zone with its own keys: PowerDNS signs the data received via AXFR itself (front-signing). The primary must deliver unsigned data for that.
set.dnssec.hint.serverReadOnly: Server “{{server}}” is set to “Save: No” – DNSSEC changes are blocked here.
set.dnssec.hint.sha1Ds: You should no longer use DS lines with digest type 1 (SHA-1) at your registrar.
set.dnssec.hint.versionUnknown: The PowerDNS version is unknown – version-dependent functions are offered without a pre-check.
set.dnssec.iterationsDanger: More than 10 iterations: many resolvers then treat the zone as insecure or return SERVFAIL.
set.dnssec.iterationsWarn: More than 0 iterations add no security and cost CPU time.
set.dnssec.keyModelCskHint: One key does both jobs; one DS record at the registrar. The best choice for most zones.
set.dnssec.keyModelKskZskHint: Classic: the KSK is registered with the registrar, the ZSK signs the records. ZSK rollovers need no registrar.
set.dnssec.keysEmpty: There are no keys for this zone.
set.dnssec.loadError: Could not load the DNSSEC status: {{error}}
set.dnssec.maxKeysReached: At most {{max}} keys per zone. Delete keys you no longer need first.
set.dnssec.narrowHint: PowerDNS computes NSEC3 answers on the fly instead of storing hashes. Saves storage, costs CPU.
set.dnssec.nsecIntro: The change takes effect immediately. PowerDNS rebuilds the chain (rectify); validating resolvers handle the switch without an outage. API-RECTIFY is switched on as well.
set.dnssec.optOutHint: Only useful for large zones with many unsigned delegations.
set.dnssec.parentDsManual: Check manually whether the parent zone still serves a DS: dig +short DS {{zone}} @1.1.1.1
set.dnssec.peerWarnBody: This zone also exists on: {{servers}}. DNSSEC is only set up on “{{server}}”. If the servers share one PowerDNS database, that is correct. With separate databases every server needs the same keys – automatic synchronisation is not included in this version (see the “Multi-server” docs).
set.dnssec.peerWarnTitle: The zone exists on several servers
set.dnssec.protect.lastActiveKey: This is the last active key. Without it the zone is no longer signed; as long as a DS exists at the registrar, validation fails. Use “Disable DNSSEC” to switch off instead.
set.dnssec.protect.lastActiveSep: This is the last active KSK/CSK. The DS at the registrar points to such a key – without it validation fails. Activate a replacement first (rollover).
set.dnssec.protect.lastPublishedSep: This is the last published active KSK/CSK. Without it in the DNSKEY RRset validation fails. Publish a replacement first.
set.dnssec.protect.parentDsPresent: The parent zone still publishes DS records for this zone. Remove them at the registrar first and wait for the TTL.
set.dnssec.rolloverAlgorithmManual: There are keys with different algorithms or active unpublished keys. An algorithm rollover works differently and is done via the key table (see the docs).
set.dnssec.rolloverComplex: The current key combination does not match a standard procedure. Please clean it up via the key table.
set.dnssec.rolloverConfirmDsAdded: The new DS is registered at the registrar and the waiting time has passed.
set.dnssec.rolloverConfirmDsRemoved: The old DS has been removed at the registrar and the waiting time has passed.
set.dnssec.rolloverDeactivateBody: The new key is active, the old one is still signing as well. Deactivate the old key now.
set.dnssec.rolloverDone: Key rollover complete. Active key: tag {{tag}}.
set.dnssec.rolloverDsAddBody: Add the DS of the NEW key (tag {{tag}}) at your registrar IN ADDITION. Do NOT remove the old DS (tag {{oldTag}}) yet.
set.dnssec.rolloverDsRemoveBody: Then remove the old DS (tag {{oldTag}}) at your registrar and wait for the DS TTL.
set.dnssec.rolloverIntro: The assistant always resumes from the current state. You can close it at any time – waiting periods keep running.
set.dnssec.rolloverKindSep: Roll the KSK/CSK (with DS change at the registrar)
set.dnssec.rolloverNoActive: There is no active key of this kind. Activate a key first.
set.dnssec.rolloverRetireBody: The old key (tag {{oldTag}}) no longer signs but stays published so cached signatures remain valid.
set.dnssec.rolloverSinceUnknown: time unknown (not done via the panel)
set.dnssec.rolloverStartBody: A new {{type}} key with {{algorithm}} is created – published but not yet active. The zone keeps being signed with the old key (tag {{oldTag}}).
set.dnssec.rolloverStepDsAdd: Add the new DS at the registrar
set.dnssec.rolloverStepDsRemove: Remove the old DS at the registrar
set.dnssec.rolloverSwitchButton: Activate new key and deactivate old key
set.dnssec.rolloverWaitDnskey: Wait at least the DNSKEY TTL (about {{ttl}}) after creation so resolvers know the new key.
set.dnssec.rolloverWaitDs: Then wait for the TTL of the DS in the parent zone (usually 1 to 24 hours; if unsure, 24 hours).
set.dnssec.rolloverWaitMaxTtl: Wait at least the largest TTL in the zone (about {{ttl}}) since the switch.
set.dnssec.rolloverZskUnavailable: Only possible with separate KSK + ZSK.
set.dnssec.saltHint: Leave empty (recommended). Hex characters 0-9/a-f only, even count.
set.dnssec.stateKeysInactive: Keys exist but none is active – the zone is not signed
set.dnssec.statePresigned: Presigned zone (PRESIGNED) – keys are not managed in the panel
set.dnssec.unchanged: No change needed – it was already in that state.
set.dnssec.warnAlgorithmPrepublishUnsigned: Note: the key uses an algorithm the zone is not yet signed with, and it is published but inactive. Strict resolvers may then treat the zone as bogus – see the “Algorithm rollover” docs.
set.zoneDetail.dnssecDisableHint: Order for switching off: first remove the DS records at your registrar, wait for the TTL (up to 24 hours), and only then disable DNSSEC here. The other way round, validating resolvers return SERVFAIL.
set.zones.dnssecRegistrarBody: Depending on your choice PowerDNS creates a CSK or KSK + ZSK. You must add the DS record at your registrar. Then open the zone details – the DS lines are in the DNSSEC card under “DS / registrar assistant” (not in the “Add record” form).
set.zones.dnssecSkippedOnServer: Zone created; DNSSEC not set up (separate database – keys only on “{{server}}”).
